header.title: Overview
header.subtitle: A comprehensive view of your organization analytics and metrics

tooltip.title: User distribution over time
tooltip.subtitle: Tracks how team composition and license utilization evolve over time
tooltip.description_1: This view shows how your team's user makeup and license usage change over time. It helps you understand who has access to your workspaces, how actively Postman is being used, and whether your available licenses are fully utilized.
tooltip.description_2: Tracking these trends can highlight growth, unused capacity, or changes in collaboration patterns.
tooltip.action_header: To manage users and licenses effectively, consider:
tooltip.action_1: Reviewing inactive users to ensure access is still needed
tooltip.action_2: Monitoring guest and partner access to maintain the right level of visibility
tooltip.action_3: Reassigning unused licenses as your team grows
tooltip.action_4: Watching changes over time to plan for future license needs

tooltip.title: Team member engagement over time
tooltip.subtitle: Understanding how users engage with your workspace helps you see how successfully people discover, onboard, and use your APIs.
tooltip.description_1: These metrics show how users interact with your workspaces and whether they're able to make successful API calls.
tooltip.description_2: Tracking engagement over time can highlight onboarding gaps, usability issues, or opportunities to improve documentation and setup.
tooltip.action_1: Reviewing onboarding content for users who make API calls but don't see successful responses
tooltip.action_2: Adding clear examples and documentation to help new users get started faster
tooltip.action_3: Monitoring trends over time to spot drops or improvements in API usage
tooltip.action_4: Comparing new users to successful users to identify where users get stuck

active_users.label: Active users

api_users.description: Users who make API calls from team workspaces, regardless of whether the response is successful.

successful_api_users.label: Successful API users

error_only_api_users.label: Error-only API users
error_only_api_users.description: Users who make API calls but receive only non-2xx responses from team workspaces.

tooltip.title: API requests by response code
tooltip.subtitle: While API Calls are good, errors are not. 4XX errors are of particular interest in Postman because they can signal friction for developers trying to onboard and test with your API. Reducing 4XX error rates will mean more developers successfully onboarding, more API calls, and happier users.
tooltip.description_1: Other errors are also captured here. However, these typically indicate technical issues within your API rather than usability problems.
tooltip.action_1: Creating an overview collection with step-by-step instructions for setting up auth
tooltip.action_2: Setting up Guided Authorization for your API domains
tooltip.action_3: Using environment variables to build the authorization into all of your requests from a single place

3xx.label: 3xx – Redirect
3xx.description: The request was sent to a different location to complete.

4xx.label: 4xx – Request error
4xx.description: There's an issue with the request, such as missing or incorrect information.

5xx.label: 5xx – Server error
5xx.description: The server couldn't process the request.

tooltip.title: Active workspaces over time
tooltip.subtitle: This chart shows how the total number of active workspaces in your team changes over time. Active workspaces include all workspaces that still exist and have not been deleted.
tooltip.description_1: Tracking active workspaces helps you understand how your team organizes work, collaborates internally and externally, and how workspace usage grows or stabilizes over time.
tooltip.description_2: An increase in active workspaces often reflects new projects or collaboration needs, while a stable or declining trend can indicate consolidation or cleanup.
tooltip.action_1: Reviewing inactive or unused workspaces to reduce clutter
tooltip.action_2: Choosing the right workspace type based on collaboration needs
tooltip.action_3: Monitoring growth trends to plan governance and access
tooltip.action_4: Ensuring workspaces are clearly named and purpose-driven

internal.label: Internal workspaces
internal.description: Refer to internal workspace that is visible to you and your team. It lets you organize your work in Postman and collaborate privately with your team.

partner.label: Partner workspaces
partner.description: An invite-only workspace for collaborating with external partners on shared API projects.

private.label: Private workspaces
private.description: A private workspace is a restricted workspace where APIs, collections, and other assets are visible only to the workspace owner and invited collaborators.

public.label: Public workspaces
public.description: Users who has made API calls and received at least one 2xx response from workspaces in team

tooltip.title: Elements in workspaces over time
tooltip.subtitle: Cumulative number of non deleted elements that exists in team as of reporting date.
tooltip.description_1: Workspaces are made up of different elements, each supporting a part of your API workflow. Viewing metrics for these elements helps you understand how your workspace is being used, where teams spend time, and which areas may need attention.
tooltip.description_2: High activity usually means an element is actively supporting development or collaboration. Low or declining activity can signal outdated setup, unused resources, or opportunities to simplify your workspace.
tooltip.description_3: Keep in mind that different elements naturally behave differently. For example, monitors run on schedules, while collections depend on manual use. Interpreting metrics in context helps you make better decisions.
tooltip.action_1: Reviewing elements with little or no activity and archiving anything no longer in use
tooltip.action_2: Checking highly used elements to ensure they're documented and easy to reuse
tooltip.action_3: Aligning environments and mocks with current development stages
tooltip.action_4: Making sure monitors and flows reflect your most important workflows

collections.label: Collections
collections.description: Groups of saved API requests you can run and reuse.

environments.label: Environments
environments.description: Sets of variables that let you switch between setups, like test and production.

mocks.label: Mocks
mocks.description: Simulated APIs that return example responses without calling a real server.

monitors.label: Monitors
monitors.description: Automated checks that run requests on a schedule to track API health.

flows.label: Flows
flows.description: Visual workflows that connect requests and logic without writing code.

header.title: Internal Workspaces
header.subtitle: View internal workspace metrics and team collaboration insights

tooltip.title: Workspaces created over time
tooltip.subtitle: This chart shows how the number of active shared and private workspaces in your team changes over time. Deleted workspaces are not included.
tooltip.description_1: An increase in workspaces can indicate growing adoption or new projects, while slower growth may suggest consolidation into existing spaces. Looking at private and shared workspaces separately provides insight into how collaboration happens across your team.
tooltip.action_header: To better understand workspace growth, consider:
tooltip.action_1: Reviewing whether new workspaces are created for clear purposes
tooltip.action_2: Encouraging shared workspaces when collaboration is needed
tooltip.action_3: Cleaning up unused or inactive workspaces to reduce clutter
tooltip.action_4: Watching trends over time to plan for team and project growth

private.label: Private workspaces
private.description: Workspaces visible only to the creator. These are often used for personal exploration, drafts, or early experimentation.

shared.label: Shared workspaces
shared.description: Workspaces accessible to multiple team members. These typically support collaboration, shared development, and team workflows.

collection_error_rates.title: Collections with the highest error rates

tooltip.title: Collections with the highest error rates
tooltip.subtitle: This view highlights collections where API requests fail most often.
tooltip.description_1: High error rates can signal issues with request setup, authentication, or API reliability, and they often point to friction for users trying to successfully use your APIs.
tooltip.description_2: Reviewing these collections helps you identify where users may be getting stuck and prioritize improvements that reduce errors and improve onboarding, testing, and overall API usability.
tooltip.action_header: To reduce error rates in collections, consider:
tooltip.action_1: Reviewing request configuration, parameters, and headers
tooltip.action_3: Adding clearer documentation or usage guidance within the collection
tooltip.action_4: Testing requests across environments to catch setup issues early

4xx.label: 4XX Errors Percentage
4xx.description: The percentage of API calls in this collection that fail due to 4XX errors.

5xx.label: 5XX Errors Percentage
5xx.description: The percentage of API calls in this collection that fail due to 5XX errors.
